candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the pollutant/parameter for this table row; a different reading of which analyte or form of manganese is referenced would change which discharge limits, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence cases are evaluated.

Without column headers, this numeric value could be an enforceable limit, a report-only threshold, or another derived quantity; treating it as a compliance limit versus a non-operative value would change whether reported measurements are compared and whether any exceedance is found.

This value appears repeatedly in the row and may represent one or more operative discharge limits; interpreting it as an enforceable numeric limit versus informational or duplicate reporting would change the applicable limit used for compliance comparison and exceedance determination.

This sentinel may mean no numeric limit, not applicable, or placeholder absence of a value; different readings would change whether an enforceable limit exists (A), whether associated monitoring or limit columns are operative (B), and whether the cell represents documented non-applicability versus unresolved missing evidence (C).

This distinct numeric entry may be a calculated or potential limit rather than a routine effluent limit; classifying it as enforceable versus analytical background would change which limit applies and whether measurements exceed it.

Like the adjacent calculated-looking value, this number could be an applicable discharge limit or a non-enforceable analytical result; the classification affects limit selection and exceedance evaluation.

Could indicate that no numeric compliance comparison applies for the corresponding column, or that monitoring/data are not required or not available; interpreting it as report-only/no-comparison versus required-but-missing evidence would change limit applicability (A) and the established missing-evidence state (C).
